title: An abstract sequence annotation hands back a mutable list
text_original: Potentially breaking: Sequences are now structured into tuples. This allows hashability, better immutability and is more consistent with the collections.abc.Sequence type. See Migrations for steps to restore legacy behavior.
text_rewritten: We annotate read-only collections with the abstract sequence type precisely because we do not want them mutated, and we put those models in dictionary keys and caches. Structuring hands back a plain list every time, so the model is unhashable and any caller can append to a field the annotation promised was read-only. The abstract annotation should produce an immutable, hashable sequence - a tuple - and the mutable annotations (the mutable sequence type and the built-in list type) should keep producing lists. This should hold for a bare call, for a field inside a model, and on both shipped converters.

acceptance_hint: Structuring against an abstract sequence annotation yields a hashable tuple with the elements converted as before, while mutable-sequence and list annotations still yield mutable lists.
